requirements.requirement: The system must include a malpractice object in the provider detail API response when malpractice data is available from the backend facade.
The system must map backend malpractice fields to the frontend schema defined in EVAL-P-MALPRACTICE-UX-S1 without field loss or renaming inconsistencies.
The system must correctly parse status values (clean, flagged, unknown) from the API response and bind them to the UI component.
The system must bind case_count, last_incident_date, state_board_url, and score_contribution fields to the UI when present in the API response.
The system must render the malpractice UI component when a valid malpractice object is present in the API response.
The system must default the malpractice status to 'unknown' when the malpractice object is present but status is null or missing.
The system must omit or hide optional fields (case_count, last_incident_date) in the UI when they are null or missing in the API response.
The system must not break the provider scorecard rendering if the malpractice object is entirely absent from the API response.
The system must display a graceful fallback message or omit the section when malpractice data is unavailable, without showing errors or placeholders.
The system must validate that the state_board_url from the API is a well-formed URL before rendering it in the UI.
The system must ensure that malformed malpractice data (e.g., incorrect types or unexpected structure) does not cause runtime UI errors.
The system must preserve neutral wording rules in the UI regardless of backend-provided text values.
The system must successfully render malpractice data end-to-end from evaluate_care_facade.py through API to UI without manual transformation outside the defined binding layer.
The system must handle API responses where malpractice fields are partially populated by rendering available data while applying fallbacks for missing fields.
